Resources and methods

The household and conversations are illustrative. National participation estimates, local research, California food rules, and the example transaction have different populations and dates.

The shopping example

The story follows a fully breastfeeding postpartum parent using California’s published no-juice package. $55 in produce benefits is separate from food quantities. The verified basket totals $22.63 before tax: $19.14 paid by WIC and $3.49 household-paid, assuming approved products and sufficient benefits. Published retailer prices were observed September 20, 2026; the story illustrates an in-store transaction, not WIC payment online.

The cabinet contains purchased groceries plus separately labeled food already at home. Benefits not purchased remain on the balance. No annual use rate or medical outcome is invented for the family.

Repeated-basket calculations use one identical basket monthly at fixed prices and continued qualifying coverage: 12 × $19.14 = $229.68; 48 × $19.14 = $918.72. These are not typical savings or the full package’s value.

Map

OpenStreetMap street geometry and an OSRM driving route were retrieved September 21, 2026. The starting point on Beverly Boulevard is illustrative, not a participant address. The route to Smart & Final #522 is 4,339.3 meters (2.7 miles). It does not establish the nearest store, traffic time, or a WIC desert. Store authorization is documented in California’s published list.
